body:
Triage: lands in `packages/plugins/plugin-security` (`bootstrap-declared-permissions.ts`) + a Setup surface → `domain:services`; type Bug (declared ≠ enforced: the artifact declares 49 grants, the env enforces the 41-grant first-boot snapshot, silently). Routed to the maintainer inbox: both asks touch stored-data/migration shape — human floor.

<!-- os-decision-facets -->
- **platform long-term coherence**: The env-authored protection is sound; the defect is the platform's *own historical rows* landing in that bucket with no exit. A one-time adoption path restores the #2705 reconcile intent without weakening provenance; leaving it means "declared = enforced" is permanently false for every rc→GA env.
- **measured business pull**: Production field report, measured on a live env — grants shipped after first boot return 403 to real users, remediation today is raw SQL. Every env upgraded along the same rc line is affected.
- **AI-agent error-resistance**: The current failure signal is a log counter — the exact silent-tolerance shape that lets drift run for weeks. Surfacing the skip loudly (Setup badge/warning on the set) is the contract-tightening half and looks safe under every option.
- **startup scope discipline**: Keep it a narrow, one-time adoption keyed on name-match + provenance-predates-scheme; do not build a general reconciliation framework.

Options: **A** boot-time auto-adoption of legacy rows matching currently-declared package sets (+ skip surfacing) · **B** explicit operator command (e.g. `os meta adopt-permission-sets`), no silent auto-migration (+ skip surfacing) · **C** document the SQL remediation only; defer.

Recommendation: **B** — auto-adoption on boot silently rewrites rows the classifier believes are admin-authored, and a name collision with a genuinely env-authored set would be destroyed without a trace; an operator-run command keeps the mutation explicit and auditable, and the skip surfacing makes the freeze visible either way. Confidence gap: this analysis cannot see how many envs sit on the rc→GA line, nor whether any genuinely admin-authored set shares a package set's name in the wild — the collision likelihood is what would flip B to A.

Related: #8672 (open, on-hold — org-less materialization, same file), #8692 (closed — seeder half). Not stamped `target:*` this round; flagged to the maintainer in the round brief instead.

Follow-up with end-to-end measurements from remediating the env — one correction and one additional mechanism.

## What remediation measured

After the operators applied the provenance/org SQL (`managed_by='package'`, correct `package_id`, `organization_id`, `active=true`) and the app was restarted, the boot sync **did** update the rows (`updated_at` bumped) — but it wrote the **same stale 43-object grants** back. The declared source it read was not the artifact.

The stale source turned out to be a `sys_metadata` row (`type='permission'`, `name='ehr_quality_inspector'`, created 2026-08-05): an admin had once **saved** this packaged permission set in the Studio permission-matrix UI, which materialized that moment's declaration as an overlay. From then on the metadata registry served the overlay instead of the shipped artifact, so every later package edit to this set was shadowed — surviving redeploys, restarts, and the provenance repair. Deleting that row (backed up first) and restarting immediately produced the correct 49-object grants for the set, and all 15 package sets reconciled to the current artifact. Chain verified byte-for-byte: overlay content (43 objects, missing the two new grants) == what the sync wrote.

## Correction to the original report

The original report attributed the freeze to the provenance skip alone. That part is now **unconfirmed for this env**: the pre-state of the provenance columns was not captured before the operators ran the repair SQL, so we cannot say whether the sync was skipping the rows or writing the overlay's stale content all along. What is measured end-to-end is that the **decisive stale source for the grant content was the `sys_metadata` permission overlay** — with provenance/org columns correct, the sync still reproduced the stale grants until the overlay was deleted. Read the issue body's provenance claim with that caveat; the two asks below stand either way.

## The additional mechanism, stated as its own hazard

A Studio-side "save" of a **package-declared** permission set creates a permanent overlay that silently shadows all subsequent package updates to that set:

- the `sys_permission_set` row's `customized` flag stayed `0` (the ADR-0094 surface an admin would check);
- the only UI trace was a generic "1 unpublished change" badge on the console home, with no link to which set, which surface, or the fact that a shipped declaration is being shadowed;
- there is no expiry, diff, or "package has moved on since this overlay was taken" signal.

For an app whose permission sets are code-managed, one accidental UI save on 08-05 froze the set's semantics for two weeks while the package shipped 6+ permission changes, surfacing only as user-facing 403s. Suggest folding this into the same asks as the issue body: surface "declared ≠ enforced" per set, and give operators a sanctioned way to discard a stale overlay (we had to delete the `sys_metadata` row by SQL).

## Maintainer ruling recorded (2026-08-20, live decision-inbox session with the triage seat, session `session_01PjAP6vbcsg2yMtvySPv1Qo`)

Ruled against the 2026-08-20 01:33Z remediation follow-up (which corrected the root-cause attribution: the decisive stale source on the affected env was a **`sys_metadata` permission overlay from an accidental Studio save**, shadowing every later package edit; the provenance-skip half is now unconfirmed there) and on the maintainer's same-day premise, verbatim: 「新项目还没上线，不需要 清理旧数据，也没有老客户升级」(the affected env is 「本地单库的企业版」, our own pilot, already hand-remediated).

**In scope (this card, `pm:queue`):**
1. **Surface "declared ≠ enforced" per set, loudly** — covering BOTH mechanisms: the provenance skip (today a log counter) and the overlay shadow (today `customized=0` plus an unlinked "1 unpublished change" badge). A package-declared set whose enforced grants differ from the shipped artifact must say so where an admin looks (Setup badge/warning naming the set and the cause).
2. **A sanctioned operator path to discard a stale overlay on a package-declared set** — the remediation had to delete a `sys_metadata` row by raw SQL; that gets a supported, audited action instead.

**Out of scope (deferred, ⛔ not built now):** boot-time auto-adoption AND the `os meta adopt-permission-sets` operator command — migration machinery for a customer population that does not exist yet. The manual SQL adoption recipe stays documented (ops doc/runbook pointer in the PR). Revisit via a fresh card when real customers sit on an rc→GA line. This supersedes both the inbox recommendation (A) and the facet block's (B) on the maintainer's premise; veto window open as usual.

⚠️ Follow-up worth its own card, filed by whoever lands this if not absorbed: the overlay-shadow mechanism itself (a Studio save of a package-declared set silently forking it from the package, `customized` flag untouched) — arguably the real product defect the field report uncovered.

State transition in the same stroke: `needs-user-decision` → `pm:queue` (`pm:blocking` retained — #8672 depends).

Reviewed PR #11533 @ `cf1c3e62d8` against the actual diff. Ruling verified on this card (2026-08-20, decision-inbox session): both in-scope asks built, the fence honoured — no boot-time auto-cleanup, per the verbatim 「新项目还没上线，不需要清理旧数据，也没有老客户升级」.

- **Surfacing covers BOTH mechanisms and the confounded shape**: `drift_status`/`drift_detail` recomputed each boot, detection independent of `managed_by`'s correctness (the active overlay is checked directly) — the exact field-reported confounded case pinned as `overlay_shadow`, not `provenance_skip`. Quiet is a data fact: in-sync persists `null`, never `'in_sync'`; steady-state re-runs issue ZERO writes (#10946 discipline, pinned).
- **The operator path is narrow, gated, and fail-closed**: tenant-admin gated endpoint; eligibility decided from the ARTIFACT REGISTRY, never `managed_by` (so the confounded row is reachable), and a name with no current package declaration is refused with no mutation — a genuinely env-authored set cannot be discarded by name collision (pinned). Heal is synchronous through the same projector the env door uses, and the healed grant set is asserted.
- **The ADR-0005 bypass is of the metadata-protocol tier-gate only, not the audit layer**: the overlay delete goes through the engine's ordinary `ql.delete` under SYSTEM context — the plugin-audit CRUD writers observe it, so the "audited" claim holds via the platform's own audit path with no bespoke audit write to drift.
- New public surface (two fields + one gated endpoint + Setup view/action) is exactly the ruled scope; clause-② discipline kept.

Verdict: PASS. Clearing `needs:contract-review` on both carriers. Enqueue/flip belongs to the dispatching seat's landing window.

## PM collection: the PASS still covers the current head — established by measurement, not assumed

The contract review (`5390095081`, fable seat, fuse read live) reviewed PR #11533 **@ `cf1c3e62d8`**. The dev has since pushed **twice** — `3e5f3825` and `95e1b45c` — to fix three CI failures. A PASS against a superseded head is not automatically a PASS on the current one, so I checked rather than assuming:

```
git diff --name-only cf1c3e62d8 95e1b45c24
  packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/permission-set-drift.test.ts
  packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/permission-set-overlay-discard.test.ts
  packages/rest/src/rest-write-response-internal-fields.tripwire.test.ts
  scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json
```

**Zero production files.** Three `.test.ts` and one gate ledger. Every surface the review actually examined — the new REST route, `drift_status`/`drift_detail`, the drift detection, the discard action's eligibility and refusal branches, and the ADR-0005 bypass it specifically adjudicated — is **byte-identical** to the reviewed state.

⇒ The PASS covers `95e1b45c`. The three follow-up pushes moved test doubles and a pin ledger, nothing the contract review was about.

### What the three fixes were, verified in source rather than taken from the report

1. **`rest-write-response-internal-fields.tripwire.test.ts`** — a `DISPOSITIONS` entry, `kind: 'no-record-echo'`, in the file's own idiom alongside `confirm`/`dismiss`/`explain`. ⭐ Its justification is *true*, not convenient: `permission-set-overlay-discard.ts:239` returns `healedRow` sourced from `tryFind` (`:216`/`:227`), and the only write verb — `ql.delete` at `:193` — has its return value discarded. There is no unstripped write mouth. No `.skip`/`.todo`/`xit` introduced.
2. **`check:engine-double-contract`** — `assertEngine*Dispatch` now present ×2 and ×3 in the two test files, `engine-double-contract.pinned.json` gained three `"pinned": 1` rows. ⛔ **`engine-double-contract.baseline.json` untouched** — the shrink-only, maintainer-only ratchet I explicitly forbade.
3. **`check:where-matcher`** — both doubles now **refuse** `$`-prefixed keys with a `throw`, matching the established idiom. The dev established the deciding fact first (neither path under test issues a combinator; they read by id/name/type/state and batch via `$in`) rather than defaulting to the quicker option, and went one level stricter by refusing unsupported operators too. ⭐ The choice is self-validating: had "never issues one" been false, the `throw` would have turned tests red.

Across three rounds of red, **neither shortcut I named was taken** — no baseline entry, no `Object.assign`/spread restatement to make the gate stop reading the double.
